title: Java Memory Model
context: What is the Java Memory Model (JMM), and why does it matter?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: The JMM defines when a write by one thread is guaranteed to be visible to another thread, and what ordering the compiler and CPU may change. Without it, a thread may see stale values held in registers or caches. The JMM defines happens-before rules: an unlock of a monitor happens-before every later lock of that monitor, a write to a volatile field happens-before a read of it, and thread start and join create ordering. Code that uses these rules is correct on every platform.

points.title: Visibility
points.why: Without synchronisation a thread may never see another thread's update.

points.title: Happens-before rules
points.why: Monitor unlock and lock, volatile write and read, and start and join create ordering.
